stop_loss_types.label: ATR-Based
stop_loss_types.description: k × ATR from entry, optionally trailing

sizing_methods.label: Fixed Quantity
sizing_methods.description: Buy a fixed number of shares

sizing_methods.label: Risk %
sizing_methods.description: Risk a fixed % of capital per trade (professional standard)

sizing_methods.label: Kelly Criterion
sizing_methods.description: Optimal sizing based on win rate and payoff ratio

indicators.name: Market Cap Bucket
indicators.description: Classifies the stock into Large Cap, Mid Cap, or Small Cap.
indicators.nse_notes: AMFI classification lists must be used historically for survivorship-bias avoidance. Must be point-in-time.

indicators.name: Price to 52W High
indicators.description: Ratio of the current price to the 52-week high, measuring how close the stock is to its yearly high.
indicators.nse_notes: Must be point-in-time computable.

outputs.name: ratio
outputs.description: Ratio of current price to 52-week high

indicators.name: Relative Volume (RVOL)
indicators.description: Compares current trading volume to its historical average over a given period.
indicators.nse_notes: Must be point-in-time computable. Essential for spotting institutional accumulation/distribution.

outputs.name: rvol
outputs.description: Ratio of current volume to average volume

indicators.name: Sector Relative Strength
indicators.description: Measures the performance of a stock relative to its sector index.
indicators.nse_notes: Sector RS is computed vs Nifty sectoral indices (e.g., Nifty Bank, Nifty IT). Must be point-in-time computable (no lookahead).

indicators.name: Awesome Oscillator
indicators.description: Indicator used to measure market momentum, calculated as the difference between a 34 Period and 5 Period Simple Moving Average.

indicators.name: Commodity Channel Index
indicators.description: Oscillator used to identify cyclical turns in commodities, equities, and currencies.

indicators.name: Moving Average Convergence Divergence
indicators.description: Trend-following momentum indicator that shows the relationship between two moving averages of a security's price.

indicators.name: Rate of Change
indicators.description: Momentum oscillator that measures the percentage change in price between the current price and the price a certain number of periods ago.
indicators.nse_notes: ROC is used for cross-sectional stock ranking in momentum investing on NSE.

indicators.name: Relative Strength Index
indicators.description: Momentum oscillator that measures the speed and change of price movements.
indicators.nse_notes: RSI 60/40 range shift is popular in Indian TA for identifying bull/bear market regimes.

indicators.name: Stochastic Oscillator
indicators.description: Momentum indicator comparing a particular closing price of a security to a range of its prices over a certain period of time.

indicators.name: Ultimate Oscillator
indicators.description: Combines short, medium, and long-term price action into one oscillator.

indicators.name: Williams %R
indicators.description: Momentum indicator that measures overbought and oversold levels.

indicators.name: Candlestick Patterns
indicators.description: Detects standard candlestick patterns.
indicators.nse_notes: Useful in Indian markets for detecting reversal points on daily and 15m timeframes.

parameters.name: pattern_type
parameters.description: Type of candlestick pattern to detect.

outputs.name: signal
outputs.description: 1 for bullish pattern, -1 for bearish pattern, 0 otherwise

indicators.name: Central Pivot Range
indicators.description: Central Pivot Range (CPR) consists of three levels: Top Central, Central Pivot, and Bottom Central. The width of the CPR indicates expected volatility.
indicators.nse_notes: CPR is hugely popular in Indian markets. A narrow CPR often signals a trending day.

indicators.name: Pivot Points
indicators.description: Calculates standard, fibonacci, or camarilla pivot points.
indicators.nse_notes: Camarilla pivots are popular among Indian index options traders.

indicators.name: Support and Resistance
indicators.description: Identifies key support and resistance levels based on swing highs/lows and PDH/PDL/PDC.
indicators.nse_notes: PDH, PDL, and PDC are highly watched levels in NSE intraday trading.

outputs.name: support
outputs.description: Nearest support level below current price

outputs.name: resistance
outputs.description: Nearest resistance level above current price

indicators.name: Aroon
indicators.description: Aroon measures whether a security is trending and the strength of the trend.

indicators.name: Average Directional Index
indicators.description: ADX measures trend strength without regard to trend direction.

indicators.name: Double Exponential Moving Average
indicators.description: Double Exponential Moving Average to reduce lag.

indicators.name: Exponential Moving Average
indicators.description: Exponential Moving Average of the price.
indicators.nse_notes: 20 EMA on 15m/Daily is widely used in Indian markets.

indicators.name: Ichimoku Cloud
indicators.description: Ichimoku Kinko Hyo is a comprehensive trend and momentum indicator.

indicators.name: Parabolic SAR
indicators.description: Stop and Reverse indicator used to determine trend direction and trailing stops.

indicators.name: Simple Moving Average
indicators.description: Simple Moving Average of the price.
indicators.nse_notes: 200 SMA is standard for long-term trend on NSE.

indicators.name: Supertrend
indicators.description: Supertrend is a trend-following indicator based on ATR.
indicators.nse_notes: Supertrend is ubiquitous in Indian retail trading. ATR period=10, multiplier=3.0 is the standard setting for BankNifty.

indicators.name: Triple Exponential Moving Average
indicators.description: Triple Exponential Moving Average.

indicators.name: Weighted Moving Average
indicators.description: Weighted Moving Average of the price.

indicators.name: Average True Range
indicators.description: Measures market volatility by decomposing the entire range of an asset price for that period.

indicators.name: Bollinger Bands
indicators.description: Volatility indicator consisting of a moving average and upper/lower bands based on standard deviation.
indicators.nse_notes: BB Squeeze before RBI policy/Budget events is a known pattern.

outputs.name: percent_b
outputs.description: %B = (Price - Lower) / (Upper - Lower). Above 1.0 = above upper band, below 0.0 = below lower band.

indicators.name: Chaikin Volatility
indicators.description: Measures the volatility by calculating the difference between high and low prices and then computing the rate of change of a moving average of this difference.

indicators.name: Donchian Channels
indicators.description: Formed by taking the highest high and the lowest low of the last n periods.

outputs.name: middle_line
outputs.description: Average of upper and lower bands

indicators.name: Historical Volatility
indicators.description: Statistical measure of the dispersion of returns for a given security or market index.
indicators.nse_notes: HV is often compared vs India VIX to determine option pricing richness.

indicators.name: Keltner Channels
indicators.description: Volatility-based envelopes set above and below an exponential moving average.

indicators.name: Delivery Volume %
indicators.description: The percentage of total traded volume that resulted in actual delivery of shares.
indicators.nse_notes: Delivery Volume % is unique to Indian markets (from NSE bhavdata). High delivery % indicates strong conviction.

outputs.name: delivery_pct
outputs.description: Percentage of traded volume marked for delivery

indicators.name: Money Flow Index
indicators.description: Money Flow Index (MFI) uses both price and volume to measure buying and selling pressure.
indicators.nse_notes: Frequently used as a volume-weighted RSI for NSE stocks.

indicators.name: On-Balance Volume
indicators.description: On-Balance Volume (OBV) measures buying and selling pressure as a cumulative indicator.
indicators.nse_notes: Used for divergence analysis in Indian midcap/smallcap stocks.

indicators.name: Volume Profile
indicators.description: Displays trading activity over a specified time period at specified price levels.
indicators.nse_notes: Helpful for identifying hidden support/resistance in Nifty/BankNifty futures.

outputs.name: poc
outputs.description: Point of Control (price level with highest volume)

indicators.name: Volume SMA Ratio
indicators.description: Ratio of current bar volume to its simple moving average.
indicators.nse_notes: Used to detect volume breakouts in Indian stocks.

outputs.name: ratio
outputs.description: Ratio of current volume to Volume SMA

indicators.name: Volume Weighted Average Price
indicators.description: Volume Weighted Average Price with optional standard deviation bands.
indicators.nse_notes: VWAP is heavily used in intraday trading. It resets at 09:15 IST on NSE every trading day.

parameters.name: deviation_multiplier
parameters.description: Multiplier for VWAP standard deviation bands

AtrBasedStop.description:
ATR-based stop-loss.

Formula:
    LONG:  stop = entry − k × ATR(period)
    SHORT: stop = entry + k × ATR(period)

When trailing=True, the stop ratchets in the favorable direction
each bar (never moves against the position).

The `k` multiplier is the single most important parameter here.
Per the spec: "k is a single, named, human-inspectable parameter —
may be optimized via backtesting (per stock or volatility bucket),
but must never be hidden inside an opaque model."

k.description: ATR multiplier. Common values: 1.5–3.0. Higher = wider stop (more room, lower win rate). This parameter is always named and inspectable.
k.title: K

trailing.description: If True, the stop ratchets in the favorable direction each bar. If False, it stays at the initial level.
trailing.title: Trailing

AtrBasedStop.title: AtrBasedStop

BacktestDefaults.description:
Default parameters for backtesting a strategy.

These can be overridden at backtest runtime, but the strategy carries
sensible defaults so it's always immediately testable.

initial_capital.description: Starting capital for the backtest (₹). Default ₹10,00,000.
initial_capital.title: Initial Capital

commission_pct.description: Commission/brokerage as a percentage of trade value. Zerodha equity delivery: 0% (but STT, exchange fees apply). Zerodha equity intraday: 0.03%.
commission_pct.title: Commission Pct

stt_pct.description: Securities Transaction Tax as a percentage. Delivery: 0.1% (buy+sell). Intraday: 0.025% (sell side).
stt_pct.title: Stt Pct

stamp_duty_pct.description: Stamp duty on buy side (0.015% for delivery, 0.003% for intraday).
stamp_duty_pct.title: Stamp Duty Pct

slippage_pct.description: Estimated slippage as a percentage of entry/exit price. Accounts for bid-ask spread and market impact.
slippage_pct.title: Slippage Pct

max_open_positions.description: Maximum number of simultaneously open positions.
max_open_positions.title: Max Open Positions

options_stt_pct.description: Options STT: 0.0625% on sell-side premium (vs 0.025% equity intraday).
options_stt_pct.title: Options Stt Pct

options_commission_flat.description: Flat brokerage per options order (₹). Zerodha charges ₹20/order for F&O.
options_commission_flat.title: Options Commission Flat

options_stamp_duty_pct.description: Stamp duty for options (0.003% on buy side).
options_stamp_duty_pct.title: Options Stamp Duty Pct

options_slippage_pct.description: Options slippage (wider bid-ask than equity). Typically 0.1%–0.3% depending on liquidity.
options_slippage_pct.title: Options Slippage Pct

wf_train_bars.description: Number of bars in the walk-forward training window.
wf_train_bars.title: Wf Train Bars

wf_test_bars.description: Number of bars in the walk-forward test (out-of-sample) window.
wf_test_bars.title: Wf Test Bars

wf_step_bars.description: Number of bars to step forward between walk-forward windows.
wf_step_bars.title: Wf Step Bars

BacktestDefaults.title: BacktestDefaults

ComparisonOp.description:
How indicator values are compared to thresholds or other indicators.

CROSSES_ABOVE and CROSSES_BELOW are stateful comparisons that require
looking at the previous bar's value — the current bar must satisfy the
condition while the previous bar must NOT have satisfied it.
ComparisonOp.title: ComparisonOp

CompoundCondition.description:
A logical grouping of conditions (AND/OR).

Supports arbitrary nesting — a compound condition can contain other
compound conditions, enabling complex multi-layered logic:

    AND(
        condition1,
        OR(condition2, condition3),
        condition4,
    )

The spec requires support for "interdependent/nested conditions
(AND/OR grouping, multi-condition combinations, e.g. daily-trend-filter
AND intraday-trigger)".

operator.description: Logical operator: AND (all must be true) or OR (any must be true).

conditions.description: Child conditions. Must have at least 2 conditions.
conditions.title: Conditions

CompoundCondition.title: CompoundCondition

ConditionOperator.description: Logical grouping operator for compound conditions.
ConditionOperator.title: ConditionOperator

EntryRule.description:
Defines how and when to enter a position.

Composed of:
- direction: LONG or SHORT
- condition: the full condition tree (leaf or compound) that must be True
- order_type: how to place the order
- optional limit offset for LIMIT orders

direction.description: Trade direction: LONG (buy first, sell later) or SHORT (sell first, buy later).

condition.description: The condition tree that must evaluate to True for entry. Can be a single LeafCondition or a nested CompoundCondition.
condition.title: Condition

limit_offset_pct.description: For LIMIT orders: offset from the signal price as a percentage. E.g., 0.1 means place the limit 0.1% below the close (for longs). Only applicable when order_type is LIMIT or STOP_LIMIT.
limit_offset_pct.title: Limit Offset Pct

strike_selection.description: Options strike/expiry selection rule. Required when the strategy's instrument_type is OPTIONS_CE or OPTIONS_PE. Defines how a directional signal is translated into a specific contract.

EntryRule.title: EntryRule

ExitRule.description:
Defines how and when to exit a position.

A position can be exited by any of:
- stop_loss: always required (risk management is non-negotiable)
- condition_exit: optional condition-based exit (e.g., RSI crosses above 70)
- take_profit: optional fixed-percentage target
- time_exit: optional time-based exit after N bars
- trailing_after_tp: convert stop to trailing after take-profit is hit

Whichever trigger fires first closes the position (or partial position
if take_profit has partial_exit_pct < 100).

stop_loss.description: Stop-loss configuration. ALWAYS required — every strategy must have a defined stop-loss.
stop_loss.title: Stop Loss

condition_exit.description: Optional condition-based exit. If set, the position is closed when this condition evaluates to True.
condition_exit.title: Condition Exit

time_exit.description: Optional time-based exit after N bars.

trailing_after_tp.description: If True, convert the stop-loss to a trailing stop after the take-profit target is hit (for partial exits).
trailing_after_tp.title: Trailing After Tp

ExitRule.title: ExitRule

FixedPctStop.description:
Fixed percentage stop-loss.

Formula:
    LONG:  stop = entry × (1 − pct / 100)
    SHORT: stop = entry × (1 + pct / 100)

pct.description: Stop-loss distance as a percentage of entry price. E.g., 2.0 means a 2% stop.
pct.title: Pct

FixedPctStop.title: FixedPctStop

FixedQtySizing.description:
Buy a fixed number of shares per trade.

Simple but flawed: doesn't account for varying share prices.
₹100/share × 100 shares = ₹10,000 vs ₹3,000/share × 100 = ₹300,000.

quantity.description: Number of shares to buy per trade.
quantity.title: Quantity

FixedQtySizing.title: FixedQtySizing

FixedValueSizing.description:
Allocate a fixed rupee amount per trade.

Position size = allocation / entry_price (rounded down to whole shares).
Better than fixed quantity but doesn't normalize for risk distance.

value.description: Rupee amount to allocate per trade (₹). E.g., 100000 means ₹1,00,000 per position.
value.title: Value

FixedValueSizing.title: FixedValueSizing

IndicatorReference.description:
A reference to another indicator's output as the comparison target.

Used for cross-indicator comparisons like:
- MACD line crosses above signal line
- Price crosses above EMA(50)
- EMA(20) > EMA(50)

The `offset` field enables "previous bar" comparisons:
- offset=0 means the current bar (default)
- offset=-1 means the previous bar

indicator_params.description: Parameter overrides for the referenced indicator.
indicator_params.title: Indicator Params

output_name.description: Which output series to reference (for multi-output indicators).
output_name.title: Output Name

timeframe.description: Timeframe override. If None, uses the same timeframe as the leaf condition this reference belongs to.

offset.description: Bar offset. 0 = current bar, -1 = previous bar, etc.
offset.title: Offset

IndicatorReference.title: IndicatorReference

InstrumentType.description:
Instrument type for the strategy.

EQUITY is the default (shares). OPTIONS_CE and OPTIONS_PE represent
F&O contracts — Call and Put options respectively.
InstrumentType.title: InstrumentType

KellySizing.description:
Kelly Criterion position sizing.

Formula:
    f* = W − (1 − W) / R

where W = win rate, R = avg_win / avg_loss (reward-to-risk ratio).

In practice, traders use Fractional Kelly (fraction × f*) to avoid
extreme drawdown volatility caused by estimation variance. Half-Kelly
(fraction=0.5) is the most common damper.

win_rate.description: Historical win rate (0 to 1, exclusive). E.g., 0.55 means 55% win rate.
win_rate.title: Win Rate

avg_win.description: Average winning trade amount (₹ or %). Must use the same unit as avg_loss.
avg_win.title: Avg Win

avg_loss.description: Average losing trade amount (₹ or %). Must use the same unit as avg_win.
avg_loss.title: Avg Loss

fraction.description: Kelly fraction (dampening factor). 1.0 = full Kelly, 0.5 = half-Kelly (recommended).
fraction.title: Fraction

max_position_pct.description: Maximum position size as a percentage of capital.
max_position_pct.title: Max Position Pct

KellySizing.title: KellySizing

LeafCondition.description:
A single indicator-based condition (the leaf of the condition tree).

Compares an indicator's output to a threshold (static value, range,
or another indicator's output).

Every field is named and inspectable — satisfying the spec's invariant
that the Strategy Builder never contains opaque/hidden logic.

indicator_id.description: The indicator to evaluate (must exist in the registry).
indicator_id.title: Indicator Id

indicator_params.description: Parameter overrides (e.g., {'period': 20}). Unspecified params use the indicator's defaults.
indicator_params.title: Indicator Params

output_name.description: Which output series to evaluate (for multi-output indicators).
output_name.title: Output Name

timeframe.description: Timeframe for this condition. If None, inherits from the strategy's primary_timeframe.

threshold.description: The comparison target — a static value, range, or indicator reference.
threshold.title: Threshold

LeafCondition.title: LeafCondition

OptionExpiry.description:
Which expiry cycle to trade.

NSE weekly options expire every Thursday; monthly on last Thursday.
OptionExpiry.title: OptionExpiry

OptionStrikeMode.description:
How the strike price is selected relative to current price.

ATM = At The Money (nearest strike to current price)
ITM_1/ITM_2 = 1 or 2 strikes In The Money
OTM_1/OTM_2 = 1 or 2 strikes Out of The Money
CUSTOM_OFFSET = user-specified offset from ATM
OptionStrikeMode.title: OptionStrikeMode

OptionsInstrument.description:
Defines a specific options contract configuration.

This is NOT a variant of an equity position — it is a distinct entity
with its own semantics (premium, lot size, expiry, strike).

instrument_type.description: CE (Call) or PE (Put). Must not be EQUITY.

strike_mode.description: How strike is selected relative to current price. ATM = nearest strike, ITM/OTM = offset from ATM.

strike_offset.description: Custom strike offset from ATM (in ₹). Only used when strike_mode is CUSTOM_OFFSET.
strike_offset.title: Strike Offset

expiry.description: Which expiry cycle to trade. Weekly options have higher theta decay but tighter premium.

lot_size.description: F&O lot size for the underlying. Auto-populated from the F&O universe if not set.
lot_size.title: Lot Size

OptionsInstrument.title: OptionsInstrument

OptionsPremiumSizing.description:
Premium-based position sizing for F&O options.

Sizes positions by premium outlay (lot_size × premium × lots),
NOT by share count. This is fundamentally different from equity
sizing because:
- Options are traded in lots (not individual shares)
- Risk is measured as premium paid, not price distance to stop
- Margin requirements differ from equity segment

Formula:
    max_lots = floor(capital × max_premium_pct / 100 / (premium × lot_size))
    lots = min(max_lots, max_lots_limit)

max_premium_pct.description: Maximum percentage of capital to deploy as premium per trade. E.g., 5.0 means risk up to 5% of capital per options trade.
max_premium_pct.title: Max Premium Pct

max_lots.description: Hard cap on number of lots per trade, regardless of capital calculation.
max_lots.title: Max Lots

max_position_pct.description: Maximum total options exposure as a percentage of capital.
max_position_pct.title: Max Position Pct

OptionsPremiumSizing.title: OptionsPremiumSizing

ParabolicSarStop.description:
Parabolic SAR trailing stop.

Uses acceleration factors that tighten the stop as the trend extends.
Not required by spec but included as a common mechanism.
ParabolicSarStop.title: ParabolicSarStop

RiskPctSizing.description:
Risk a fixed percentage of capital per trade.

Formula:
    position_size = (capital × risk_pct / 100) / (entry − stop)

This is the professional standard. Ensures equal rupee risk per trade
regardless of stock price or volatility. REQUIRES a stop-loss to be
defined (the validation engine enforces this).

Example: Capital ₹10,00,000, risk 1% (₹10,000), entry ₹500, stop ₹480.
Risk per share = ₹20. Position = 10,000 / 20 = 500 shares.

risk_pct.description: Percentage of total capital to risk per trade. Professional standard: 0.5% to 2.0%.
risk_pct.title: Risk Pct

max_position_pct.description: Maximum position size as a percentage of capital, regardless of the risk calculation. Prevents concentration.
max_position_pct.title: Max Position Pct

RiskPctSizing.title: RiskPctSizing

StaticRange.description:
A fixed numeric range for BETWEEN comparisons.

Example: RSI BETWEEN 30 and 70 → StaticRange(low=30, high=70)
StaticRange.title: StaticRange

StaticValue.description:
A fixed numeric threshold.

Example: RSI > 70 → StaticValue(value=70)
StaticValue.title: StaticValue

StrikeSelectionRule.description:
Named, inspectable rule that translates a directional signal
into a specific options contract.

When the strategy generates a bullish signal → buy CE with the
configured strike/expiry. When bearish → buy PE.

All parameters are visible and configurable as toggles in the UI
(consistent with invariant: Strategy Builder never contains a
black-box model).

bullish_instrument.description: Which instrument to trade on a bullish signal. Default: buy a Call (CE).

bearish_instrument.description: Which instrument to trade on a bearish signal. Default: buy a Put (PE).

strike_mode.description: Strike selection: ATM, ITM, OTM, or custom offset.

strike_offset.description: ₹ offset from ATM strike. Only used when strike_mode is CUSTOM_OFFSET.
strike_offset.title: Strike Offset

expiry.description: Expiry cycle: current/next weekly or monthly.

min_premium.description: Minimum acceptable premium (₹). Filters out too-cheap (illiquid) options.
min_premium.title: Min Premium

max_premium.description: Maximum acceptable premium (₹). Prevents overpaying for deep ITM options.
max_premium.title: Max Premium

StrikeSelectionRule.title: StrikeSelectionRule

SwingLowStop.description:
Swing-low (or swing-high for shorts) stop-loss.

The stop is placed at the most recent local price minimum (for longs)
or maximum (for shorts), with an optional buffer.

Per the spec: "most recent local price minimum, with a lookback window
long enough to capture a genuine prior swing, not recent noise."

lookback_bars.description: Number of bars to search for the swing low/high. Must be long enough to capture a genuine prior swing (not recent noise). Minimum 5 bars enforced.
lookback_bars.title: Lookback Bars

buffer_pct.description: Buffer below the swing low (or above swing high for shorts) as a percentage. Prevents stop from sitting exactly at the swing level where clusters of stops may exist.
buffer_pct.title: Buffer Pct

SwingLowStop.title: SwingLowStop

TakeProfitConfig.description:
Take-profit configuration.

Defines a target exit price as a fixed percentage above entry (for longs)
or below entry (for shorts).

pct.description: Take-profit distance as a percentage of entry price. E.g., 4.0 means a 4% target.
pct.title: Pct

partial_exit_pct.description: Percentage of the position to exit at the target. 100.0 = full exit, 50.0 = exit half at target.
partial_exit_pct.title: Partial Exit Pct

TakeProfitConfig.title: TakeProfitConfig

TimeBasedStop.description:
Time-based stop — exit after N bars if no other exit is hit.

Prevents capital from being tied up in stagnant positions.

max_bars.description: Maximum number of bars to hold the position. E.g., 6 bars on 15-min chart = 90 minutes max hold.
max_bars.title: Max Bars

TimeBasedStop.title: TimeBasedStop

TimeExitConfig.description:
Time-based exit — close position after N bars.

Used to prevent capital from sitting in stagnant trades.
Can be combined with stop-loss and take-profit.

max_bars.description: Maximum number of bars to hold the position.
max_bars.title: Max Bars

TimeExitConfig.title: TimeExitConfig

Timeframe.description:
Candle/bar timeframe.

Includes M75 (75-minute) which is NSE-specific: the NSE trading session
runs 09:15–15:30 IST = 375 minutes. A 75-min candle produces exactly
5 clean candles per day with no partial-candle distortion (unlike 60-min
which produces 6 full + 1 partial 15-min candle).
Timeframe.title: Timeframe

UniverseFilter.description:
Defines how the stock universe is filtered before strategy execution.

The Confidence Scanner's output feeds into this: e.g., "only consider
stocks scoring above +60". This links Module A (prediction) to
Module B (execution) without coupling them.

min_confidence_score.description: Minimum confidence score from the Confidence Scanner. E.g., 60 means only consider stocks scoring ≥ +60.
min_confidence_score.title: Min Confidence Score

max_confidence_score.description: Maximum confidence score (for short strategies, e.g., only stocks scoring ≤ −60).
max_confidence_score.title: Max Confidence Score

watchlist.description: Explicit list of stock symbols to consider (e.g., ['RELIANCE', 'TCS']). If set, only these stocks are evaluated.
watchlist.title: Watchlist

sector_filter.description: Limit to specific sectors (NSE sectoral index names). E.g., ['NIFTY BANK', 'NIFTY IT'].
sector_filter.title: Sector Filter

market_cap_filter.description: Limit to specific market cap buckets. E.g., ['LargeCap', 'MidCap'].
market_cap_filter.title: Market Cap Filter

min_avg_volume.description: Minimum average daily volume (number of shares) over the lookback period. Filters out illiquid stocks.
min_avg_volume.title: Min Avg Volume

min_avg_turnover.description: Minimum average daily turnover (₹) over the lookback period.
min_avg_turnover.title: Min Avg Turnover

fno_only.description: When True, pre-filters the universe to F&O-eligible stocks only (~200 symbols). Required for options strategies. (Invariant #7: no options signal for non-F&O stocks.)
fno_only.title: Fno Only

volume_lookback_days.description: Number of days to average volume/turnover over.
volume_lookback_days.title: Volume Lookback Days

UniverseFilter.title: UniverseFilter

VolatilityAdjustedSizing.description:
ATR-normalized position sizing.

Formula:
    position_size = (capital × risk_pct / 100) / (k × ATR)

Normalizes risk across high-beta and low-beta equities by sizing
inversely to volatility.

risk_pct.description: Percentage of total capital to risk per trade.
risk_pct.title: Risk Pct

k.description: ATR multiplier defining the risk unit.
k.title: K

max_position_pct.description: Maximum position size as a percentage of capital.
max_position_pct.title: Max Position Pct

VolatilityAdjustedSizing.title: VolatilityAdjustedSizing

body.description:
The canonical, versioned, machine-readable strategy configuration.

This is the single source of truth. Both the toggle UI and the NL chatbot
read and write to instances of this model. There is no separate code path.

Every field is named and inspectable (spec invariant #3). The strategy
can be serialized to JSON, validated, versioned, and diffed.

body.name: Market Cap Bucket

body.description: Ratio of the current price to the 52-week high, measuring how close the stock is to its yearly high.
body.nse_notes: Must be point-in-time computable.

outputs.description: Ratio of current price to 52-week high

body.name: Relative Volume (RVOL)
body.description: Compares current trading volume to its historical average over a given period.
body.nse_notes: Must be point-in-time computable. Essential for spotting institutional accumulation/distribution.

body.name: Sector Relative Strength
body.description: Measures the performance of a stock relative to its sector index.
body.nse_notes: Sector RS is computed vs Nifty sectoral indices (e.g., Nifty Bank, Nifty IT). Must be point-in-time computable (no lookahead).

body.name: Awesome Oscillator
body.description: Indicator used to measure market momentum, calculated as the difference between a 34 Period and 5 Period Simple Moving Average.

body.name: Commodity Channel Index
body.description: Oscillator used to identify cyclical turns in commodities, equities, and currencies.

body.name: Moving Average Convergence Divergence
body.description: Trend-following momentum indicator that shows the relationship between two moving averages of a security's price.

body.name: Rate of Change
body.description: Momentum oscillator that measures the percentage change in price between the current price and the price a certain number of periods ago.
body.nse_notes: ROC is used for cross-sectional stock ranking in momentum investing on NSE.

body.name: Relative Strength Index
body.description: Momentum oscillator that measures the speed and change of price movements.
body.nse_notes: RSI 60/40 range shift is popular in Indian TA for identifying bull/bear market regimes.

body.name: Stochastic Oscillator
body.description: Momentum indicator comparing a particular closing price of a security to a range of its prices over a certain period of time.

body.name: Ultimate Oscillator

body.name: Williams %R
body.description: Momentum indicator that measures overbought and oversold levels.

body.name: Candlestick Patterns
body.description: Detects standard candlestick patterns.

outputs.name: signal

body.name: Central Pivot Range

body.nse_notes: CPR is hugely popular in Indian markets. A narrow CPR often signals a trending day.

body.name: Pivot Points

body.nse_notes: Camarilla pivots are popular among Indian index options traders.

body.name: Support and Resistance

body.nse_notes: PDH, PDL, and PDC are highly watched levels in NSE intraday trading.

outputs.name: resistance

body.name: Aroon
body.description: Aroon measures whether a security is trending and the strength of the trend.

body.name: Average Directional Index
body.description: ADX measures trend strength without regard to trend direction.

body.name: Double Exponential Moving Average
body.description: Double Exponential Moving Average to reduce lag.

body.name: Exponential Moving Average
body.description: Exponential Moving Average of the price.
body.nse_notes: 20 EMA on 15m/Daily is widely used in Indian markets.

body.name: Ichimoku Cloud
body.description: Ichimoku Kinko Hyo is a comprehensive trend and momentum indicator.

body.name: Parabolic SAR
body.description: Stop and Reverse indicator used to determine trend direction and trailing stops.

body.name: Simple Moving Average
body.description: Simple Moving Average of the price.
body.nse_notes: 200 SMA is standard for long-term trend on NSE.

body.name: Supertrend
body.description: Supertrend is a trend-following indicator based on ATR.
body.nse_notes: Supertrend is ubiquitous in Indian retail trading. ATR period=10, multiplier=3.0 is the standard setting for BankNifty.

body.name: Triple Exponential Moving Average
body.description: Triple Exponential Moving Average.

body.name: Weighted Moving Average
body.description: Weighted Moving Average of the price.

body.name: Average True Range
body.description: Measures market volatility by decomposing the entire range of an asset price for that period.

body.name: Bollinger Bands
body.description: Volatility indicator consisting of a moving average and upper/lower bands based on standard deviation.
body.nse_notes: BB Squeeze before RBI policy/Budget events is a known pattern.

outputs.description: %B = (Price - Lower) / (Upper - Lower). Above 1.0 = above upper band, below 0.0 = below lower band.

body.name: Chaikin Volatility
body.description: Measures the volatility by calculating the difference between high and low prices and then computing the rate of change of a moving average of this difference.

body.name: Donchian Channels
body.description: Formed by taking the highest high and the lowest low of the last n periods.

outputs.name: middle_line
outputs.description: Average of upper and lower bands

body.name: Historical Volatility
body.description: Statistical measure of the dispersion of returns for a given security or market index.
body.nse_notes: HV is often compared vs India VIX to determine option pricing richness.

body.name: Keltner Channels
body.description: Volatility-based envelopes set above and below an exponential moving average.

body.name: Delivery Volume %
body.description: The percentage of total traded volume that resulted in actual delivery of shares.
body.nse_notes: Delivery Volume % is unique to Indian markets (from NSE bhavdata). High delivery % indicates strong conviction.

body.name: Money Flow Index
body.description: Money Flow Index (MFI) uses both price and volume to measure buying and selling pressure.

body.name: On-Balance Volume
body.description: On-Balance Volume (OBV) measures buying and selling pressure as a cumulative indicator.
body.nse_notes: Used for divergence analysis in Indian midcap/smallcap stocks.

body.name: Volume Profile
body.description: Displays trading activity over a specified time period at specified price levels.
body.nse_notes: Helpful for identifying hidden support/resistance in Nifty/BankNifty futures.

outputs.name: poc

body.description: Volume Weighted Average Price with optional standard deviation bands.
body.nse_notes: VWAP is heavily used in intraday trading. It resets at 09:15 IST on NSE every trading day.

parameters.name: deviation_multiplier
parameters.description: Multiplier for VWAP standard deviation bands

strategy_summary.stop_threshold: Exit signal fires at P(exit better) ≥ 62%
strategy_summary.how_it_works: At every held minute the AI evaluates current price behaviour, volume, momentum, Greeks and time-of-day. It predicts two things: (1) P(exiting NOW beats waiting) — if ≥ 62% → exit immediately (stop or peak). (2) How tight to trail the stop below current price — tighter when momentum is weakening or volume reversing, looser when trend is strong. The trailing stop can only move UP. Exit when price falls below it.
strategy_summary.summary: Dynamic exit AI (accuracy 73.4%). Exit-signal driven by: time_fraction, minutes_held. Trail tightness driven by: volume_1m, time_fraction.
